Decant

Ambient RNA decontamination for single-cell and single-nucleus RNA-seq, with a differential expression test that models ambient RNA instead of subtracting it. No other ambient RNA tool we found offers one.

Documentation: the User Guide covers installation, the Seurat workflow, multi-sample data, differential expression and diagnostics, chapter by chapter.

What is new

  1. Contamination-aware differential expression (ambient_de(), DecantDE()). When disease tissue releases more ambient RNA than controls, an abundant cell type’s disease genes leak into every other cell type and are reported as differentially expressed. Existing tools correct counts and then test. Decant puts each sample’s measured ambient RNA, and its uncertainty, inside the negative binomial model: mu = native expression + ambient. It supports covariates and is robust to outlier samples in large cohorts. Status: experimental. With shuffled labels on three real datasets it now rarely reports false hits, a little more often than standard edgeR; it has not yet been shown to beat a standard test on real data (see Limits).
  2. Correction that keeps what cannot be ambient (bayes_cell). Counts far above what ambient RNA could produce in a cell (doublets, rare expressers) keep their molecules; only the expected ambient share is removed.
  3. Never adds counts. Corrected counts are bounded by the observed counts, checked on every run.
  4. Ambient-aware ligand-receptor calls (chirp()). A ligand made by the cell type that dominates the soup is detected in every cluster, so the usual detection rule makes every cluster look like a sender. chirp() calls a gene in a cluster only when its count is well above what ambient RNA would put there, and scores pairs on the excess. Status: experimental, simulation only (see Limits).
  5. Every default is gated. Each component must pass a falsification test against ground truth in CI. Components that failed are kept off and documented.

How it compares

Correction against experimental ground truth

Two datasets from the benchmark of Cargnelli et al. (2026), scored with the paper’s metrics. Retain is the share of the cell’s own signal that is kept, and removal the share of ambient signal removed, both per gene, 1 is best. Decant, SoupX and DecontX were run on the same inputs. CellBender’s numbers are the paper’s own, not a run here.

Decant SoupX DecontX CellBender (published)
human/mouse mixture 20k: retain 0.989 0.992 0.983 0.996
human/mouse mixture 20k: removal 0.616 0.345 0.722 0.729
held-out mixtures 1k, 5k, 10k: retain (mean) 0.992 0.982 0.984 not run
held-out mixtures 1k, 5k, 10k: removal (mean) 0.444 0.679 0.637 not run
Smart-seq2, no ambient RNA: retain 0.998 0.989 0.952 0.797

Decant removes less ambient RNA than DecontX: 10 points less on the 20k mixture and 19 points less on held-out mixtures, where its contamination estimate is too low. It keeps more of the cells’ own counts than DecontX and SoupX. It removes almost nothing where there is nothing to remove. Its contamination estimate now matches the cross-species truth (median 0.027 against 0.029; before this release 0.013). That mixture was used to find the estimator’s flaw; results on held-out mixtures are in validation/BENCHMARK.md, sections 1c and 1d.

Opt-in alternative: correction = "bayes_absent". It decides, gene by gene and cluster by cluster, whether a gene is expressed at all, and removes all counts of genes that are not. On two 10x mixtures never used in its design (pre-registered), it removed 0.891 of ambient signal against DecontX’s 0.655 and the default’s 0.531. The cost is retain: 0.9918 against DecontX’s 0.9920 and the default’s 0.9945. That missed the pre-stated bar, so it is not the default (validation/BENCHMARK.md, sections 1g and 1h). Use it when removing ambient RNA matters more than the last fraction of a point of native signal.

Correction: six tools on real 10x PBMC 4k data

Same cells, soup and clusters for every tool. “Ambient-compatible” foreign counts are marker counts in cell types that do not express the marker, at a level ambient RNA could explain; “not ambient” are those too high to be ambient, mostly B-cell doublets. A good tool removes the first and keeps the second.

Decant SoupX DecontX CellBender¹ AmbiDose scAR
ambient-compatible foreign counts removed 88–95% 76–94% 97–100% 54–98% 67–79% 99–100%
counts that are not ambient removed (lower is better) 14–37% 12–31% 96–100% 4–68% 82–100% 58–82%
native marker signal lost 1–4% 1–2% 2–6% 0–1% 0–6% 18–26%
counts added 0 0 0 0 0 727,390
run time (4 CPU cores) 11 s 12 s 34 s 55 min 73 s 15 min

¹ Reduced CPU configuration; CellBender is designed for a GPU.

Decant removes more ambient-compatible counts than SoupX and AmbiDose on all three marker sets and than CellBender (as run here) on two of three. It keeps the counts that are not ambient, which DecontX, AmbiDose and scAR remove, and it is as fast as the fastest tool. DecontX removes 5 to 9 points more of the ambient-compatible counts. Details and caveats: validation/BENCHMARK.md.

Differential expression (simulated case/control studies)

leaked genes called (of 80), 6 vs 6 null false-positive rate, 6 vs 6 null false-positive rate, 50 vs 50, confounding batch
ambient_de 0 0.05 0.05
SoupX, then edgeR 1.5 0.04 not run
naive edgeR 53 0.22 0.45
naive Wilcoxon not run not run 0.46
subtract ambient, then Wilcoxon not run not run 0.14

Nominal false-positive rate 0.05. In the 6 vs 6 study, correcting with Decant’s bayes rule and then running edgeR was as good as ambient_de; ambient_de is the option that stays valid with covariates such as batch.

Calibration on real data. Condition labels shuffled between donors so that there is nothing to find, 24 shuffles per cell type. A calibrated test reports a hit in a few shuffles, and few genes when it does.

data, cell types ambient_de: shuffles with a hit most hits in one shuffle naive edgeR: shuffles with a hit
GSE272082 brain, AD vs control; microglia, oligodendrocytes 4 of 48 9 1 of 48
GSE190015 brain, nine controls; microglia, oligodendrocytes 5 of 48 1 3 of 48
GSE273597 pancreas, T1D vs control; acinar 1 of 24 1 0 of 24
GSE273597 pancreas; ductal 4 of 24 (before this release: 5, up to 2,300 genes) 1 0 of 24
GSE273597 pancreas; alpha 6 of 24 5 4 of 24

On the pancreas data, for 6 of 23 donors the ductal ambient fraction came out at 0.86 to 0.96 (the others 0.02 to 0.16): a single cell type’s pseudobulk cannot always identify its own ambient fraction. The model treated most of those donors’ counts as soup, and splits that separated them gave over a thousand false hits. ambient_de now replaces a value above max_rho (0.5) with the median of the other samples, adds their spread to its uncertainty, and warns. That removed the false hits; it changed nothing on the two brain datasets. The pancreas data were used to find the problem, so they do not show the guard works elsewhere. ambient_de is slightly more liberal than naive edgeR overall (hits in 20 of 168 shuffles against 8, never more than 9 genes). Details: validation/BENCHMARK.md, sections 3b and 3c.

An earlier problem, the cause of hits in most shuffles on the brain data (82 of 96 tests, up to 574 genes), was fixed by using edgeR’s trended dispersion (section 3b).

Install 

remotes::install_github("kroy3/Decant")

Quick start

The raw (unfiltered) matrix is required: its empty droplets measure the ambient RNA.

library(Decant)
raw <- read_10x_counts("sample/outs/raw_feature_bc_matrix")
cells <- colnames(read_10x_counts("sample/outs/filtered_feature_bc_matrix"))
d <- split_droplets(raw, cells = cells)
res <- decant(d$cells, d$empties, clusters = my_clusters)
res$corrected   # corrected counts, sparse
res$rho         # per-cell contamination

From Seurat:

obj <- RunDecant(obj, raw = "sample/outs/raw_feature_bc_matrix")  # new "Decant" assay

res <- DecantDE(obj, cell_type = "Microglia", sample_col = "donor",
                formula = ~ diagnosis, raw = raw_paths_by_donor)
subset(res, ambient_driven)   # hits a standard pipeline reports that the soup explains

Limits

  • Ground truth so far is four human/mouse mixtures and one negative control, all from cell lines. On the 10k mixture Decant underestimates contamination (0.021 against 0.062) and ranks cells poorly; DecontX does better there. The genotype mixture and the paper’s medium- and high-complexity datasets are not yet run.
  • When the soup resembles the cells (a single cell type), contamination cannot be estimated from expression. Decant then warns and asks for rho; the number it reports in that case is not reliable.
  • Memory: about 9.5 GB for 11,000 cells and 1.9 million empty droplets.
  • ambient_de() is experimental. On real data it has been checked for calibration only (three datasets, shuffled labels); before this release it failed in pancreas ductal cells. That it removes ambient-driven hits a standard test reports is shown only in simulation, from a simulator that follows the model’s own mechanism. Two pre-registered real-data tests (pancreas, T1D vs control; brain regions within donors) could not show it: the standard test found no ambient-driven hits to remove (validation/BENCHMARK.md, 3c and 3d). Until there is real-data evidence, report ambient_de hits together with a standard pseudobulk test. Analyses made with earlier versions should be rerun.
  • chirp() is experimental and untested on real data. On simulated data it made no false sender calls where the 10% detection rule made 608-944 and correcting with bayes_cell first still left 70-388. The simulator matches its model, CellChat and CellPhoneDB were not run, and it misses most pairs expressed at 5-20 per 10k. It relies on rho; with rho at half its true value it made up to 100 false calls.
  • Empty droplets that over-represent genes the cells also express are not detected and make the contamination estimate too low.

The full scorecard, design notes and history are in validation/SCORECARD.md; changes are in NEWS.md.
